transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm not overreacting by being here, and I don't want to waste your time. It's probably just normal stress, but... well, I've been having these really bothersome thoughts lately. I'm sorry, I want to make sure I'm explaining this right. 

I just keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I've missed something critical. Like, at work—I deal with data and numbers a lot—I'll suddenly panic that I put a wrong number in a data release. Or even just normal things at home, I'll suddenly think I left the back door unlocked, or paid a bill from the wrong account. And the thing is, I know I checked it. I really do. But my mind just... it won't let go of the possibility that I've caused some kind of terrible disaster. 

It sounds so silly and irrational when I say it out loud, I know... I'm sorry. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help with?

When you have these intrusive thoughts, do you feel driven to perform certain actions or rituals—like checking things repeatedly, counting, or trying to 'undo' the thought in some way—to reduce the anxiety they cause?

Yes, that's... that's exactly it. You really understand what I'm trying to say. I, um... I feel a little embarrassed admitting this, because I know I should just be able to let it go, but... yes. 

To try and calm myself down, I do end up checking things. Probably more than I should. At work, I'll... I'll reopen spreadsheets I've already closed and saved, or I'll reread my emails line by line. And at home, it's the locks, or pulling up payment confirmations on my phone over and over. I kind of have to do it in a set order, just until my mind finally feels like it's 'safe.' I hope that doesn't sound too ridiculous? 

I really just want to be thorough and do a good job, but... well, it gets a bit out of hand. Some nights, I'm still sitting at my desk hours later, and I haven't actually finished anything new because I've just been reviewing the same data. I'm so sorry, I know how terribly inefficient that sounds for someone in my line of work. Is that... is that the kind of behavior you were asking about?
